title: Indigo Pike Solutions
text:
Indigo Pike Solutions

Inbound SMB lead via self-serve signup — trial started 2026-02-24. Small engineering team (mobile/web SDKs); building a conversational support widget + document q/a. They picked Hosted API (self-serve) initially — public cloud only, no VPC for now.

Key technical pain (primary reason for discovery call): problems when using streaming + function/tool-calling + JSON mode. Symptoms reported: 
- Streaming deltas arrive as fragments that are not valid JSON until stream end -> their client-side JSON parser throws and resets the session.
- On some runs, model emits function_call with args that don't match the declared schema (extra fields or array vs object) -> their function runtime rejects call.
- Edge case: trailing commas and stray newline characters in the streamed JSON chunks cause strict parsers to fail.
- They also see occasional 'function_call' being emitted as plain text in non-function mode when prompt includes an instruction to call external tools.

What we did on call (2026-03-03, 35m, FF id ff-20260303-9231):
- Walked through streaming behavior: explained that streaming sends incremental tokens; client must assemble and parse only complete objects. Recommended using a tolerant chunk-assembler that accumulates until top-level JSON braces balance OR using Redwood's structured output helpers (content-type: application/json + json_mode).
- Demonstrated use of official SDK streaming helper that emits 'delta' events and a final 'complete' signal; they were not buffering finalization correctly.
- Discussed function schema enforcement: recommended sending explicit function definitions in the request, ensure 'name' matches exactly, and validate args with a lightweight schema guard before invoking their tool. Showed example where model returns stringified JSON for args vs actual JSON object — advised setting function param types and using 'always_call' when you want deterministic function-first behavior.
- Logged two repro captures they shared (RDW-4129) and provided initial notes to engineering.

Customer quotes / persona notes: "We love the latency but our frontend parser is brittle — if any chunk is malformed the whole widget crashes." CTO (Ava) wants a small pairing session to replay a failing trace. Product lead (Noah) is sensitive to cost but values predictable behavior; prefers Hosted API if we can close streaming reliability.

POC / next milestones:
- Short-term: 1-hour pairing between Jordan (SE) + Riley (AE) + Indigo Pike engs to replay failing stream (target week of 2026-03-15). Need sample request with headers, streaming mode flag, and raw delta messages.
- Mid-term: push a small SDK example + guidance doc on streaming + function_call best practices for their frontend team. Attach sample code snippets in drive:/deals/indigopike/streaming-guides.md.
- Long-term: potential expansion to Dedicated if heavy usage and stricter SLAs required; not in plan right now.

Suggested sales messaging: emphasize easy onboarding (self-serve credits), streaming SDK helpers, and a short technical pairing to remove blockers. Highlight cost controls (token monitoring) since they are cost-sensitive.

Open questions for engineering: which tokenization behavior leads to arrays vs objects in function args? Are we emitting any stray whitespace/newlines in streaming boundary messages? Capture: RDW-4129 (support ticket) contains two raw streams from 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-02.

Short CRM-style timeline (bullets):
- 2026-02-24: self-serve signup + credit applied (trial).
- 2026-02-25: initial onboarding email (owner: Riley Park).
- 2026-03-01: customer raised JSON parse failures via support form -> RDW-4129 created.
- 2026-03-03: discovery call (FF ff-20260303-9231) — demo + repro collection.
- 2026-03-10: SE provided streaming checklist + initial guidance (drive links).
- 2026-03-12: follow-up; customer agreed to pairing session week of 2026-03-15.

Next steps (as of 2026-03-12): pairing session scheduled; Jordan to request raw streaming logs and full request payloads. Blocker remains frontend parser fragility + unclear function schema mismatch.
